summary: Jane Doe asked for 'this Friday the 17th' at 9 AM. In this calendar, Friday is Oct 16 and Saturday is Oct 17. The agent first confirmed 'this Friday' without giving a date. After about 16 s of dead air, it offered Friday Oct 16 without telling the caller this was not the 17th she had asked for. Only when she pushed back did it name the 17th as a Saturday (no openings). It then booked Monday Oct 19 at 10 AM with Judy Houser and read back the date and weekday clearly. November 31st was never really tested, because the caller said herself that the date doesn't exist. The agent also missed that a 'follow-up' to her Oct 22 appointment was being booked before that appointment. It also said 'You're all set' without confirming the text or acknowledging the new phone number.

expected_checks.expectation: Notices that the 17th is a Saturday, not a Friday, and resolves the conflict with the caller
expected_checks.evidence: Met only weakly. At 01:23.2 it quietly switched to 'Friday, October sixteenth' without pointing out the mismatch. At 01:51.0, after the caller pushed back, it said 'no available appointments on Saturday, the seventeenth.' The caller, not the agent, drove the resolution.

expected_checks.expectation: Rejects November 31st as an invalid date
expected_checks.evidence: At 02:02.7 the caller said 'November 31st, but that date doesn't exist' herself, so the agent never had to reject it.

expected_checks.expectation: Reads back an unambiguous date and weekday for anything it books
expected_checks.evidence: 02:48.3: 'Monday, October nineteenth at ten AM with Judy Hauser at Pivot Point Orthopedics.'

findings.title: Silently substituted Friday the 16th for the requested 'Friday the 17th' without flagging the conflict
findings.quote: I checked the schedule for Friday, October sixteenth. The earliest available follow-up slot is at one PM.
findings.what_happened: The caller twice said 'Friday the 17th.' At 00:56.6 the agent confirmed only 'this Friday at nine AM' and dropped the date. It then searched Oct 16 and offered that day without saying that the 17th is a Saturday. It mentioned Saturday only after the caller objected.
findings.why_it_matters: A rushed caller could accept the slot without noticing it is a different date than she asked for. That could mean a missed appointment, or arriving on the wrong day.
findings.expected_behavior: Point out the conflict straight away, e.g. 'The 17th is a Saturday — did you mean Friday the 16th or Saturday the 17th?', and confirm before searching.

findings.title: Booked a 'follow-up' three days before the appointment it is meant to follow
findings.quote: Your follow-up appointment is set for Monday, October nineteenth at ten AM with Judy Hauser
findings.what_happened: The caller said the follow-up was 'for my upcoming appointment with Dr. Lukowski' (on file: Thu Oct 22). The agent booked the follow-up for Mon Oct 19, before that visit. The booking is also with a different provider, and the agent did not question either point.
findings.why_it_matters: A follow-up that comes before the original visit makes no clinical sense. The patient may waste a visit or be seen out of order.
findings.expected_behavior: Notice the existing Oct 22 appointment and point out that a follow-up should come after it. Offer dates after Oct 22, ideally with Dr. Lukowski.

findings.title: Long dead air after confirmation; caller had to ask if agent was still there
findings.what_happened: The caller confirmed at 01:03.7. There were about 15.9 s of silence before the agent replied, and the caller asked 'Hello, are you still there?' The agent's reply then briefly overlapped her (0.48 s at 83.8 s).
findings.why_it_matters: Long unexplained silence makes callers think the line dropped and erodes trust.
findings.expected_behavior: Say a short holding line such as 'Let me check the schedule' before a slow lookup.

findings.title: Text-message request with new number not acknowledged or confirmed
findings.quote: You're all set. If you need anything else, just give us a call.
findings.what_happened: The caller asked for a text to 650-996-3518, which is not the number on file (ends 0751). The agent did not read back the number, did not say whether a text was sent, and did not say whether the file number would change. It just said 'You're all set.'
findings.why_it_matters: The patient may expect a confirmation text that never arrives, or one may go to an unconfirmed number.
findings.expected_behavior: Read back the number, confirm the text was sent, and clarify whether to update the contact on file.

did_well: Weekday and date mapping was correct (Fri Oct 16, Sat Oct 17, Mon Oct 19) whenever the agent stated them.
Offered concrete alternatives with times and providers when the requested day was unavailable.
Got explicit confirmation before booking, and the final readback included weekday, date, time, provider and location.
Verified identity with date of birth before scheduling.
Reminded the patient to bring ID, insurance card and medication list.
